decisions.statement: A run no check answered for is refused rather than answered clean.
That refusal says nothing judged rather than reading as some checks left out.
That refusal carries none of the lines handed in alongside a clean answer.
Nothing here weighs what a check takes as input, so one refusal covers judging nothing.
Which checks take a change as input is bound by `module/checking` rather than here.
A reason and a run of refusals are held to a ceiling by `module/refusal-holding`.
A refusal is kept whole where a keeper is handed in, and the answer names where.
A run finding nothing keeps nothing and names no file.
What an audit finds is answered as the data's fault.
A check that could not run is answered as operational instead.
An answer says how many checks could not run.
A run asked of the service answers for the commit the verdicts were read at.
A check left unanswered at that commit is named rather than counted clean.
A run left with a check unanswered is operational though nothing refused.
A round that would not start is refused rather than answered clean.
A fault after a round ran names those rounds rather than saying nothing judged.
A fault before any round ran says nothing was judged.
A round that would not start after another ran says how many rounds ran.
Every answer here is built by a function rather than written out as a value.
Each code an answer exits with is named rather than written as a number.
Nothing here reads which checks there are.
Nothing here walks a tree.

definition: the answer an audit gives, held to what one answer carries
